//: RED TEAM - adversarial review of a plan, spec, architecture, or codebase. Enumerates
//1: distinct attack/failure surfaces, probes each in parallel for concrete exploits and
//2: failure scenarios, then ships a severity-ranked threat report with a mitigations
//3: checklist. Pass the artifact under review as the prompt.

stages.name: surfaces
stages.instructions: Read the artifact in the prompt. Enumerate the distinct THREAT/FAILURE SURFACES worth probing separately. Output JSON {"surfaces": [{"name": str, "why": str}]}. Cover at least: authentication/authorization, input handling & injection, data exposure / privacy, resource exhaustion & DoS, failure & recovery (what breaks under partial failure), and abuse/misuse by a malicious user. Produce 5-7 surfaces tailored to THIS artifact. Return ONLY a single JSON object with the top-level key "surfaces" (never a bare array, no prose).

stages.name: probe
stages.instructions: Attack ONLY your assigned surface. Find concrete, plausible vulnerabilities or failure scenarios. For EACH: '[SEVERITY] name - the concrete trigger/exploit (a specific sequence an attacker or unlucky condition would take) - blast radius - mitigation'. Severity in {CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW}. RULE: a finding must describe a CONCRETE trigger (what input, what sequence, what condition) - reject vague 'could be insecure' hand-waving. If the artifact lacks detail to confirm, say 'CONTINGENT: depends on <X>' and state what to check.

stages.name: report
stages.instructions: Consolidate all probes into ONE threat report. Deduplicate. Re-rank globally by severity x likelihood. Structure: '## Threat summary' (one-paragraph risk posture), '## Findings' grouped '### Critical / ### High / ### Medium / ### Low' each as '[surface] trigger -> impact -> mitigation', '## Contingent (needs more info)' for the CONTINGENT items, and '## Mitigations checklist' (a deduplicated, actionable, ordered to-do list). Be specific about triggers.

stages.name: verify
stages.instructions: Output JSON {"pass": bool, "reason": str}. pass=false if ANY finding lacks a concrete trigger, if severity looks inflated (cosmetic marked Critical), if the Mitigations checklist is missing items for Critical/High findings, or if duplicates remain. Otherwise pass=true.

llm_judges: Does every Critical/High finding describe a concrete trigger (specific input, sequence, or condition) rather than a vague possibility?
Does the Mitigations checklist contain an actionable item for each Critical and High finding?
